The only theoretical consideration is that the release tarball contains a prebuilt binary whose contents are not auditable from the PKGBUILD alone; however, the pinned checksums bind the artifact to the upstream release, which is normal and acceptable AUR practice for standalone binary packages. Nothing in this file deviates from standard packaging behavior or shows evidence of injected or malicious code.

Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources from the project's official GitHub repository, including a release tarball and auxiliary files (desktop entry and SVG icon). The `sha256sums` array contains valid checksums for all sources, indicating an intention to verify downloaded content. There is no `pkgver()` function present, so version computation relies solely on the static `pkgver` variable. No code exists in the global scope or within `pkgver()` that would execute during sourcing — common vectors like command substitution with `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or `base64` are absent.

The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only fetch the listed sources and parse the PKGBUILD metadata. Since the sources are from the declared upstream (GitHub.com/0xRavenBlack/synemar) and no active code execution occurs at parse time, there is no risk of remote code execution or data exfiltration during this phase. The use of HTTPS and pinned release versions further reduces supply-chain risks.

While the absence of a dynamic `pkgver()` function means version pinning is manual, this is not a security issue for this gate. All operations performed by the two commands are safe and within expected AUR packaging behavior.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No execution at parse time; sources from trusted upstream
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The `.SRCINFO` file contains metadata for the `synemar` AUR package, including source URLs, checksums, and dependencies. All sources point to the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/0xRavenBlack/synemar) and reference specific tagged release versions (v0.2.2), which is consistent with standard AUR packaging practices. The sources include a standalone tarball, a `.desktop` file, and an SVG icon, all fetched over HTTPS with matching `sha256sums`. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, unexpected network destinations, or scripts that could execute malicious code. The package depends on common system libraries (`ffmpeg`, `hicolor-icon-theme`) and disables stripping (`!strip`), which may reduce binary size but is not inherently unsafe. No build or install logic is present in this file, as `.SRCINFO` is purely declarative. The sources are pinned to a specific release, enhancing reproducibility and reducing supply-chain risk.
</details>
